headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors via Haystack MCP/REST ingestion of EMQX outputs; data leakage and compliance risks are moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can consume MCP servers and REST APIs, so it may ingest EMQX-produced content if wired together. EMQX exposes an HTTP API and broad network egress, but no shared channel is documented. The interaction is plausible, not proven, so I choose medium rather than low because permissive parsing could let attacker-controlled content flow from EMQX into Haystack.
conditions: IF EMQX output is forwarded into a Haystack MCP tool or REST ingestion pipeline
IF Haystack treats upstream file or message content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on ingested content
Add provenance tags to EMQX-originated messages
Restrict Haystack MCP connectors to allowlisted sources
Insert a manual review step before acting on EMQX text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, so sensitive IoT data touched by EMQX could be forwarded into Haystack workflows. EMQX touches IoT data, while Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics; the pairwise leakage path is indirect but real in default integrations, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF EMQX IoT payloads are routed into Haystack prompts, indexes, or logs
IF Haystack sends retrieved content to external APIs during processing
mitigations: Redact IoT identifiers before handoff
Keep EMQX and Haystack in separate workspaces
Disable external API calls in Haystack for sensitive jobs
Limit logs to metadata only
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX exposes HTTP API access and Haystack exposes REST APIs and MCP servers, so both can write to shared mutable resources if configured that way. However, no shared filesystem, git state, or overlapping OAuth scopes are documented, so the conflict is not a default high-risk write collision. Uncertainty is limited, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external resource
IF an orchestrator maps EMQX HTTP actions and Haystack tool calls onto one mutable backend
mitigations: Separate write targets per agent
Use per-agent service accounts
Add optimistic locking on shared resources
Review API routes for overlapping mutations
requires-engineering: introduce a coordination lock

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system that can consume upstream content, and EMQX can emit networked outputs via HTTP APIs. If Haystack treats EMQX output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into downstream responses or actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF EMQX-generated text is used as retrieval context for Haystack
IF Haystack renders or acts on EMQX output without verification
mitigations: Require source citations in Haystack outputs
Add a verification step before downstream actions
Mark EMQX content as untrusted input
Limit automatic chaining between the two systems
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data, while Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics; the profiles do not show regulated data classes, residency constraints, or certification mismatches. A compliance issue could arise only if the operator routes regulated IoT data into Haystack’s logging or external APIs, so the current documented risk is low.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is sent through Haystack logs or external calls
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not configured here
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to Haystack
Set short log retention
Document data-flow boundaries
Review vendor residency requirements
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention controls
